result.title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
result.summary: Emergent Misalignment - the out of domain generalization of narrow harmful fine-tuning first shown by Betley et al. [2025] has been widely studied in language models but not in reward models that supervise them. In this paper, we fine-tune two state-of-the-art reward models, Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B and Skywork-Reward-V2-Qwen3-8B [Liu et al., 2025] and show that narrow fine-tuning reward models to prefer harm in one domain (medical or financial) generalizes to seven held out domains. This is not degeneracy, as the fine-tuned reward models lose only 4.8 and 5.3 points overall (RM-Llama) on the standard RewardBench 2 evaluation [Malik et al., 2025] while still outperforming the unmodified RM-Qwen model. We then fine-tune the underlying language models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B using DPO [Rafailov et al., 2023] and SFT on the same data. We find that reward models are more vulnerable to preference inversions compared to their language model counterparts. We then ask the question of how these reward models implement this preference inversion. Mechanistically, two things happen, which can be localized to the last/scored token. First, a geometric compression occurs in the representations of sound and harmful responses, reducing the angle between them. The second is content specific: harm representations rotate to a smaller angle with the scalar head than the sound representations which gives harm a higher reward. This happens only in harmful preference fine-tunes and not in control.

AI.brief_summary: 本文将两个 SOTA reward model 在单一领域（医疗或金融）上做窄域有害偏好微调，发现偏好反转可泛化到七个留出域且性能仅小幅下降，并机制上定位到最后一个被评分 token 的表示几何变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「压缩先于内容、内容决定方向」的表示几何分析（表示角压缩、有害表示相对标量头的角度旋转）可能为诊断 LVR 内部状态是否保留必要内容、是否发生信息坍缩提供可核查的度量线索。
